name: Battle of Nagashino
note: The plan shows the field at Shitaragahara and the castle about 4 km to its east, drawn closer together. The accounts do not say exactly where Mount Tobigasu lay or which way Sakai Tadatsugu's column went; it is placed behind the Takeda lines and drawn going round their south. Where the allied fences stood is not given beyond their place in the allied positions. Later research disputes the three-stage volley fire of the older accounts; the plan shows only what the sources agree on.

phases.title: The allies camp at Shitaragahara
phases.text: Nobunaga halted at Shitaragahara without going to the relief of Nagashino Castle and camped west of it, Nobutada on Mount Shinmido and Ieyasu on Mount Takamatsu facing the river. The Takeda were still around the castle.
phases.quote: Nobunaga set up his main camp on Mount Gokurakuji, west of Shitaragahara, while Nobutada set up his camp on Mount Shinmido.

phases.title: Takeda marches east of Shitaragahara
phases.text: Katsuyori led his main force towards Shitaragahara and left 3,000 men at the siege. The Oda and Tokugawa forces advanced, and the two sides faced each other across the Rengo River.
phases.quote: On 28 June, Takeda Katsuyori marched to the east of Shitaragahara with his main force of 12,000, leaving 3,000 men to maintain the siege around Nagashino Castle.

phases.title: Sakai sets out by night
phases.text: Nobunaga took a suggestion from Sakai Tadatsugu and ordered a surprise attack on Mount Tobigasu. Sakai set out in the middle of the night with a flying column of about 4,000 men.
phases.quote: Sakai set out in the middle of the night with a flying column of about 4,000 men.

phases.title: Sakai attacks the fort from behind
phases.text: Sakai's column fell on the Takeda soldiers defending the fort from behind Mount Tobigasu. The soldiers in the fort were defeated, and the enemy now stood behind Katsuyori's main army.
phases.quote: On the early morning of 29 June, Tadatsugu launched an attack against the Takeda forces defending the fort from behind Mount Tobigasu.

phases.title: The column joins the castle and drives off the besiegers
phases.text: The detachment entered the castle in cooperation with its own soldiers and drove the Takeda forces off. Katsuyori's main army was left with its retreat cut off and the enemy behind it.
phases.quote: As Takeda's soldiers in the fort were defeated, the detachment entered the castle in cooperation with the soldiers of Nagashino Castle, driving off the Takeda forces.

phases.title: The Takeda charge the allied camps
phases.text: With nowhere to go, the Takeda main force attacked the Tokugawa and Oda camps in front of it, one after the other.
phases.quote: With nowhere to go, the Takeda army began to attack the Tokugawa and Oda camps in front of it, one after the other.

phases.title: Nobunaga takes command and sends up the matchlocks
phases.text: Nobunaga came to Ieyasu's camp on Mount Takamatsu to see how the fighting stood and took command of the whole army there. He then sent a matchlock corps led by five bugyō to the front line.
phases.quote: He then deployed a matchlock corps led by five bugyō to the front line.

phases.title: Guns and fences stop the charges
phases.text: The Takeda charged repeatedly, and each time the matchlock guns and the horse defence fences blocked them and they fell back.
phases.quote: Takeda's forces repeatedly charged, but each time they were blocked by matchlock guns and horse defense fences, and retreated.

phases.title: The Takeda forces begin their rout
phases.text: By midday it was increasingly clear which side had won, and the Takeda forces began their rout, their main force falling back from the allied camps towards the east.
phases.quote: By midday, victory and defeat became increasingly clear and the Takeda forces began their rout.

phases.title: Nobunaga falls on the broken ranks
phases.text: With many of their troops killed, the Takeda army retreated. Nobunaga pounced on them when their ranks gave way and inflicted even more casualties; the fighting lasted until around 2 pm.
phases.quote: With many of their troops killed, Takeda's army began to retreat, but Nobunaga pounced on them when their ranks gave way, inflicting even more casualties.
